rounds.text: Allcargo Global Ltd carries severe fundamental and balance sheet risks that are not supported by its depressed profitability metrics. The company suffers from an alarming debt burden, with borrowings surging to Rs 2,358 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 1,338 Cr a year earlier, driving the debt-to-equity ratio up to an unhealthy 1.83x where debt exceeds net worth [E23, E25]. This high leverage is compounded by a low interest coverage ratio and a troubling flag that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E42, E44]. Furthermore, short-term liquidity is compromised as the current ratio sits below parity at 0.91x, meaning current liabilities exceed current assets [E24]. Operational and return metrics are deeply negative, highlighted by an atrocious trailing twelve-month profit growth of -1468% and a miserable return on equity of -20.1% [E12, E14]. These deteriorating fundamentals manifest in a stretched valuation via an EV/EBITDA of 22.81x, which heavily outstrips the sector benchmark of 10.46x [E10]. Investors also face extreme equity volatility of 81.3% alongside a negative Sharpe ratio of -0.89 and a worst historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.5% [E36, E37, E35]. Conceded: the company demonstrates positive operating cash flow of Rs 89 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 86 Cr in March 2026, alongside an increasing quarterly operating margin trend over the last five quarters [E19, E21, E22].
